summary: Round 2, prose only (ADR-0044, an amendment to ADR-0043's Status, two research banners, corrected javadoc on SubscriptionEvent and SubscriptionEventGrantTest, M5.66, M5.45f done). No production logic; no object-store request added, moved or authorised on any path this diff touches. ⚠️ THE STAGED BYTES CHANGED UNDER ME MID-REVIEW: the packet I was handed hashes to 59a3363a29f5, the tree now hashes to 14d57da9dfff (ADR-0044 226 -> 230 lines, M5.66's row rewritten). EVERY FINDING BELOW WAS RE-VERIFIED AGAINST THE CURRENT BYTES, and two findings I had written against the packet are now genuinely closed by that edit and are NOT reported: M5.66 now carries a criterion 4 naming security.md rule 3 by name and by standard, and its criterion 2 now asserts REQUESTS as well as bytes, at the unfavourable share, naming the 401-against-1 runs-per-node shape and non-negotiable 6 -- which is the cost defect I was going to raise against that row. THREE ROUND-1 FINDINGS ARE PROPERLY CLOSED. R1: doc 04 §2c carries a further banner retiring all three claims by name, including the span [0, max(byteStart+byteLen)), checked against ADR-0043:69-77 and against SegmentReader.open's footer-first order. R5: the @param grant wording now matches the compact constructor exactly -- read, not assumed: it refuses a grant with SESSION_EPOCH_ABSENT (:245), a range with no grant (:249), a half range (:256), a non-positive length and a negative start, and NOTHING refuses a grant on an INLINE event, while SubscriptionHub.Push guards both directions at HEAD:101-108. R2 is closed for SubscriptionEventGrantTest -- 'It does.' is retracted and replaced by 'IT DOES NOT', matching Decision (c). Counted facts checked rather than taken: client/build.gradle.kts declares exactly api(project(':format')); check-module.sh:234 NO_HTTP is 'format binstore-spi sequencer ingest' and :236 NO_CLOUD is 'client plugin'; no src/main backend declares presign. All true. BUT THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION I WAS ASKED IS STILL YES -- A CORRECTION LANDED IN ONE OF TWO PLACES THREE MORE TIMES, AND ONE OF THEM IS THE SWEEP TABLE ITSELF ASSERTING A SITE WAS EXAMINED WHEN THE SECOND HIT IN THAT FILE CONTRADICTS THE DISPOSITION. (1) The sweep dispositions research doc 13 as 'the segment directory again'; doc 13:110 is the SUBSCRIPTION EVENT carrying byteStart/byteLen beside via, under :103 asserting the directory is never read on the hot path because exact byte ranges are pushed -- the claim this record retires -- and doc 13 carries no banner anywhere. (2) The doc 10 banner went on §8 and left §7:182, 'merge adjacent ranges before requesting, in every mode', standing -- the one line in the corpus that is an instruction to the client implementer, and a line ADR-0044 QUOTES in alternative (b1) as live corpus design while Decision (b) establishes no range is expressible. (3) Rule 3's handoff reached M5.66 and doc 04 but not ADR-0043, which still reads 'rule 3's range half has no owner' (:122) and 'NOT CARRIED by any of the new rows' (:213-216) -- both now false, and both explicitly left standing by the new Status line's 'on decision (b)'s JUSTIFICATION only'. And the number R4 asked for does not follow from the record's own inputs: 7 bytes on a ~100-byte event where every event carries one is ~7% of the stream and ~52x the segment figure, not '~2%' and '15x' -- and ~2% is the figure the record tells a reader to quote.

findings.title: The sweep dispositions research doc 13 as 'the segment directory again'; doc 13's other two hits are the SUBSCRIPTION EVENT and a sentence asserting exactly the claim this record retires
findings.summary: The row reads '`format/…/SegmentReaderTest.java`, research docs 01 §3, 03, 13 | **Not this question** — the segment directory again, same as the RunEntry row'. That is true of doc 01:60-61 (the 48-byte RunEntry drawing) and of doc 13:96 (the same directory inside a table). It is FALSE of doc 13's other two sites: :103, 'On the hot path **none of them is read**: the ingester pushes exact byte ranges' — 'them' includes the stream directory — and :108-112, the push-event sketch '{ index, partition, firstOffset, recordCount, segment: "…-h76800-…bseg", byteStart: 184320, byteLen: 65536, via: "inline" | "proxy" | "direct" }', which is the subscription event and not the directory. Doc 03:153 is a third structure again — the commit log's per-stream section — not the segment directory either. Doc 13 carries no revision banner anywhere in the file; grepped.
findings.failure_scenario: This is the round-1 blocking finding one document over. Doc 13 is the corpus's 'whole path once, concretely, with the request counts' page, and the research skill routes a reader there for exactly the end-to-end question M5.66 and M5.45g/h ask. Its taker reads that the event carries byteStart/byteLen and that on the hot path the directory is never read because the ingester pushes exact byte ranges, and builds the consumer that acts on those coordinates — the prefix or union span SegmentReader.open refuses with 'segment is truncated: no footer magic' on every delivery, since ConsumerClient.decodeInto opens the whole array with no partial path. They will not re-check, because the sweep table in an accepted ADR records doc 13 as examined and irrelevant. That is worse than the omission round 1 found: criterion 3 demanded a per-site disposition precisely so 'corrected' could be told from 'not looked at', and this row says 'looked at' about lines that were not.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the row. Doc 01 §3 and doc 13 §4's table row stay 'not this question'. Doc 13 §4:103 and §5:108-112 get their own row plus a banner in doc 13 saying the consumer's read is whole-object, that SegmentReader reads the directory on every decode in every mode, and that the event's copies are consumed by no reader (M5.66). Give doc 03:153 its own line — it is the commit log's coordinates, a third structure, and calling it the segment directory is the same error one notch smaller.

findings.title: The doc 10 banner landed on §8 and left §7's 'merge adjacent ranges before requesting, in every mode' standing — the one corpus line that is an instruction to a client implementer
findings.summary: §7 lists the client library's responsibilities and :182 reads '**Read coalescing** — merge adjacent ranges before requesting, in every mode.' ADR-0044 knows this line: alternative (b1) quotes it verbatim as evidence 'the corpus also designed for ranges throughout' and uses that to reject removal — while Decision (b), three paragraphs earlier, establishes that no range is expressible at all. The banner this commit adds sits at :207 under §8, speaks only about degradation paths, and mentions neither coalescing nor §7; the ADR's Research header scopes the correction to '§8's degradation claim', and the sweep row for this file says '§8 | Corrected, revision banner' and nothing about §7.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.45h is the row that implements read coalescing, and doc 10 §7 is the corpus page for the client library's responsibilities — the first place its taker reads. They find a numbered responsibility telling them to merge adjacent ranges before requesting, in every mode, with no banner on it; §8's banner is under a different heading about a different claim. They union the K events' byteStart/byteLen and issue one ranged GET, which carries no footer, and SegmentReader.open throws 'segment is truncated: no footer magic' before a record decodes — the defect M5.45b round 2 measured and this record exists to bury. It is also an internal contradiction in ADR-0044: a claim it retires in (b) is leaned on in (b1) to reject the alternative it calls the closest call.
findings.suggested_fix: Banner §7:182, or extend the §8 banner to name it: the merge is of DELIVERIES, not of byte ranges — one whole-object GET per (node, segment), M5.45h — because no ranged request is expressible. And drop or qualify the §7 citation in alternative (b1), which argues from the retired claim.

findings.title: Rule 3's handoff to M5.66 reached the backlog row and doc 04 but not ADR-0043, which still says the clause has 'no owner' and 'is NOT CARRIED by any of the new rows' — sentences the new Status line explicitly leaves standing
findings.summary: Three sites now say M5.66 owns security.md rule 3's range half: ADR-0044:157-175, doc 04 §2c's new banner, and SubscriptionEventGrantTest's javadoc; the mid-review edit added M5.66's criterion 4, so the receiving row carries it too. ADR-0043 does not. :113-122 still reads 'whether one ever becomes fillable is M5.45f's to settle. Either way rule 3's range half has **no owner**', and :213-216 still reads 'The range half of security.md rule 3 that this record leaves open is NOT CARRIED by any of the new rows … M5.45f owns whether a range ever becomes fillable'. Both are false as of this commit — M5.45f is marked done here and does not own it, and M5.66's criterion 4 carries it. The Status amendment this commit adds is scoped in its own words to 'decision (b)'s JUSTIFICATION only' and says only that the reopening is closed, which actively tells a reader the rest of decision (b), including the 'no owner' sentence, still stands.
findings.failure_scenario: ADR-0041:114 is where security.md rule 3's range half is first deferred, and it hands off through this record; anyone auditing that clause — the next security pass, or M5.20's sweep — lands on ADR-0043, reads 'no owner' and 'NOT CARRIED by any of the new rows', follows 'M5.45f owns' to a row marked done in this very commit, and concludes either that M5.45f closed the clause (Decision (c) says explicitly that it did not) or that it is unowned and opens a duplicate row. ADR-0044's own words for that state are 'worse than leaving it visibly open'. This is the one-of-two-places defect inside the single file criterion 2 named: the amendment landed at the top and the sentences it falsifies are 115 and 200 lines down, marked out of scope by the amendment's own wording.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the Status amendment by one clause — the ownership sentences at :122 and :213-216 are superseded too: rule 3's range half is owned by M5.66, criterion 4 — since the Status block is already the mechanism this record uses to correct that file and its current scope line is what excludes them.

findings.title: The subscription-stream figure R4 asked for does not follow from the record's own inputs: ~2% and '15×' should be ~7% and ~52×, and ~2% is the one it tells a reader to quote
findings.summary: :84-97 states 7 bytes per event carrying a range, 1,600 events naming one segment, and 11,200 bytes total — i.e. every event carries one — then 'an event is on the order of 100 bytes with a 48-byte URL, so the range is nearer **7% of an event and ~2% of that stream** — roughly 15× the segment-denominated figure. Both are true and the second is the one a reader should quote'. When every event carries the range, the per-event share and the stream share are the same number: 11,200 / (1,600 × 100) = 7.0%, and 7.0% / 0.1335% = ~52×, not 15×. The two figures in one sentence need two different event sizes (~100 bytes for the 7%, ~350 bytes for the 2%); they cannot share a denominator.
findings.failure_scenario: Decision (b) rejects (b1) on price — 'keeping them is close to free' — and records (b1) as 'the closest call in this record'. The figure it names authoritative understates the share of the channel these bytes actually travel on by ~3.5×, so the next reader re-weighing keep-versus-remove — M5.66's owner, whose criterion 3 requires revisiting Decision (b), and whose criterion 1 must derive a crossover — re-prices a close call from a number that is not derivable from the paragraph it sits in, or notices the two percentages contradict and cannot tell which was intended. The heading over it is 'THE NUMBER, because an alternative rejected without one is an assertion'; a wrong number there is worse than the missing one round 1 flagged, because it reads as derived.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one event size and let both percentages fall out of it. At the stated ~100 bytes it is ~7% of an event and ~7% of the subscription stream, ~52× the segment-denominated 0.13%. If the intended size is a real v3 event (a ~48-byte URL plus a ~45-byte segment key puts it nearer 150-200 bytes), state that size and recompute both — the defect is the two figures sharing one sentence and not one denominator.

findings.title: Decision (c) — the answer to round 1's major — sits physically inside '## Alternatives considered', formatted identically to the rejected (b1)/(b2)/(b3)
findings.summary: '## Decision' is :44 and holds (a) :46 and (b) :67. '## Alternatives considered' is :108 and holds (a1) :110, (a2) :119, (a3) :125, (b1) :132, (b2) :144, (b3) :149 — and then (c) at :157, before '## Consequences' at :176. (c) is a decision, is lettered like one, and is the only place in the tree that states rule 3's range half is not closed.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader checking what this record decided about security.md rule 3 reads the Decision section, finds (a) and (b) and no (c), and concludes the record did not address it — the state round 1 blocked on. A reader who does reach :157 finds it among options whose siblings each open with 'Rejected'. Low blast radius: the paragraph is unambiguous once read, which is why this is minor.
findings.suggested_fix: Move (c) to follow (b) under '## Decision'. Pure cut-and-paste; nothing references it by line.

findings.title: 0.13% is the only figure quoted at every other site this commit writes the price, immediately after the record says that denominator is not the one to quote
findings.summary: ADR-0044:91-97 names two denominators and says 'the second is the one a reader should quote'. Every other site written in this diff quotes the first and only the first: SubscriptionEvent.java:121 'priced carrying them at 0.13% of the segment they describe'; backlog M5.45f's State cell '11,200 bytes against an 8,388,608-byte segment: 0.13%'; backlog M5.66 'priced at 0.13% of the segment they describe'; ADR-0044:138 and :191, the last as a bare 'a cost of 0.13%'.
findings.failure_scenario: The field javadoc is, in this record's own words, 'where a reader looks'. Someone weighing whether the two fields earn their place reads 0.13% there or in M5.66's row and never reaches the paragraph calling that denominator the misleading one, so the decision is re-made on the figure the record deprecates. Minor because 'of the segment they describe' is an accurate qualification wherever it appears; :191's bare form is the one that is not. It turns from deprecated into wrong if finding M5.45f-r2-4 is fixed.
findings.suggested_fix: Nothing, if it lands with this recorded in the commit body (rule 11). If touched at all, touch it once — the stream-denominated figure in the javadoc, in M5.66's row and at :191 — so the price reads the same in all four places.
